topic: The Barber Pole Effect: Optically Active Sugar Solutions
target_audience: University Physics students or curious high school science enthusiasts

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Polarized Light Filter
lecture_lines: Light behaves like a transverse wave.
A polarizer acts as a picket fence.
Only one polarization plane passes through.
animations: Create a circular polarizer, labeled #FFEB3B 'Polarizer'. Position it at Row B, Column 5.
Animate light waves passing through the Polarizer, turning orange #FF9800. Position the wave at Row D, Column 5.
Show the light wave oscillating vertically, labeled #2196F3 'Intensity'. Position the label at Row D, Column 4.

sections.title: The Phenomenon of Optical Rotation
lecture_lines: Chiral molecules act on polarized light.
Sugar solutions physically twist the polarization plane.
This rotation is called optical activity.
animations: Create a test tube liquid, labeled #8BC34A 'Solution'. Position at Row B, Column 5.
Animate the rotation of the light wave color #FF9800 clockwise through the solution. Position at Row D, Column 5.
Animate the rotation angle, labeled #E91E63 'Theta'. Position at Row D, Column 4.

sections.title: Creating the 'Barber Pole' Effect
lecture_lines: Different wavelengths rotate by different angles.
Two polarizers selectively block specific colors.
The result looks like a rotating barber pole.
animations: Display multiple vertical light beams, labeled #FFFFFF 'Beams'. Position at Row B, Column 5.
Rotate the beams slowly to create a spiral #9C27B0 'Pole'. Position at Row D, Column 5.
Highlight the overlap region between beams, labeled #FFFFFF 'Twist'. Position at Row D, Column 4.

sections.title: Mathematical Visualization (Malus's Law)
lecture_lines: Malus's Law dictates the light's final intensity.
Intensity follows an I zero cos squared theta pattern.
Changing concentration shifts the intensity curve.
animations: Draw Malus's Law formula I = I0 cos^2(theta), labeled #FFC107 'Eq'. Position in Row D, Column 5.
Animate a slider, labeled #00BCD4 'Angle'. Position in Row B, Column 5.
Dynamically change the intensity bar color based on 'Angle'. Position bar in Row E, Column 5.

sections.title: Application: The Saccharimeter
lecture_lines: Chemists use this to measure sugar concentrations.
The saccharimeter works like a light-based scale.
It reveals liquid purity through optical rotation.
animations: Create a sugar solution vessel, labeled #795548 'Sample'. Position in Row B, Column 5.
Pass light through sample and measure angle, labeled #FFEB3B 'Rotation'. Position in Row D, Column 5.
Display result on a scale, labeled #FFFFFF 'Concentration'. Position in Row E, Column 5.
